title: Closed support as a relative section complex
statement:
Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion,
with complementary open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow T$.
For a complex $K$ of etale $A$-module sheaves,
there is a natural isomorphism of ordinary derived
$A$-module complexes

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*A_D,K)
\cong\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(R\Gamma(T,K)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(V,v^*K)\bigr)[-1].
$$

proof.text: Write $A_T,A_D,A_V$ for the constant coefficient ring sheaves (the commutative-ring convention of the derived-category definition). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to the $A_T$-module $A_T$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $v^{-1}A_T=A_V$ and $i^{-1}A_T=A_D$, canonically. Thus obtain $0\to v_!A_V\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A_T\xrightarrow{\eta}i_*A_D\to0$ in $A_T$-modules, with the adjunction counit and unit as its maps. This result applies to arbitrary open complements, with no finite-type hypothesis on $v$.

source.place: Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; constant coefficient inverse image as in Modules on Sites, Tag 04JC

proof.text: The category $\Mod(T_{\Et},A)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] in that category to choose a functorial quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and each $I^n$ injective. Put $C^n=\Hom_T(i_*A_D,I^n)$, $E^n=\Hom_T(A_T,I^n)$, and $B^n=\Hom_T(v_!A_V,I^n)$, with differentials given by postcomposition with $d_I$. These are $A$-module complexes; the global Hom-complex convention is [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

Applying $\Hom_T(-,I^n)$ to the sequence of step 1 gives $0\to C^n\to E^n\xrightarrow{q^n}B^n\to0$: a morphism vanishing on $v_!A_V$ factors uniquely through its cokernel $i_*A_D$, and surjectivity of $q^n$ is exactly the extension property defining the injective object $I^n$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Postcomposition with $d_I$ commutes with precomposition, so these are a short exact sequence of complexes. The adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies $B^n$ with $\Hom_V(A_V,v^*I^n)=\Gamma(V,v^*I^n)$, and $E^n=\Gamma(T,I^n)$: a module map out of the rank-one constant ring sheaf is determined by the image of $1$, and a section $s$ defines the map $a\mapsto as$. These identifications commute with $d_I$. The counit formula in the adjunction node shows that $q$ is precisely restriction of sections, not an unspecified map between these complexes.

source.place: Tags 095L and 03S4; Modules on Sites Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero

proof.text: The restriction $v^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and is right adjoint to the exact functor $v_!$ by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] says that $v^*I$ is K-injective, while exactness makes $v^*K\to v^*I$ a quasi-isomorphism. Step 2 also applies with $V$ in place of $T$, so both sheaf categories have enough K-injectives. The K-injective computation [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] identifies $E=\Gamma(T,I)$ with $R\Gamma(T,K)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,v^*I)$ with $R\Gamma(V,v^*K)$ on the whole unbounded derived categories. Here termwise global sections, followed by localization to $D(A)$, is an exact functor on the homotopy category: it commutes with finite direct sums, shifts and the displayed cone differential. The same computation applied to $\Hom_T(i_*A_D,-)$ identifies $C$ with ordinary global $R\Hom_T(i_*A_D,K)$; termwise Hom from this fixed degree-zero sheaf likewise commutes with shifts and cones. Step 3 identifies the derived restriction morphism with $q:E\to B$.

Use the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The complex $\operatorname{Cone}(q)[-1]$ has degree-$n$ term $B^{n-1}\oplus E^n$ and differential $(b,e)\mapsto(-d_Bb-q(e),d_Ee)$. The map $C\to\operatorname{Cone}(q)[-1]$, $c\mapsto(0,c)$, is a chain map and a quasi-isomorphism, as follows directly from degreewise surjectivity of $q$. For a cocycle $(b,e)$, choose $a\in E^{n-1}$ with $q(a)=-b$; subtracting the boundary of $(0,a)$ leaves $(0,e-d_Ea)$ with $e-d_Ea\in C^n$. Conversely, if $(0,c)$ is the boundary of $(b,e)\in B^{n-2}\oplus E^{n-1}$, then $q(e)=-d_Bb$; choose $a\in E^{n-2}$ with $q(a)=b$, and $e+d_Ea\in C^{n-1}$ has differential $c$. Thus the map induces bijections on every cohomology group. It is natural for chain maps $I\to I'$, since it is just inclusion into the second summand. The functorial resolution from step 2 therefore gives naturality in $K$ at the complex level. To descend this naturality to derived categories, let $f:K\to K\prime$ be a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the resolution maps gives $I(f)\eta_K=\eta_{K\prime}f$, so $I(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] it is a homotopy equivalence. More explicitly, a homotopy $h:I^n\to (I\prime)^{n-1}$ with $f_I-g_I=d_{I\prime}h+hd_I$ induces homotopies $h_C,h_E,h_B$ by postcomposition, and $q\prime h_E=h_Bq$. On the shifted cones the degree-minus-one map $H(b,e)=(-h_Bb,h_Ee)$ satisfies $dH+Hd=(f_B-g_B)\oplus(f_E-g_E)$: the off-diagonal term is $-q\prime h_E+h_Bq=0$, and the diagonal terms are $d_Bh_B+h_Bd_B$ and $d_Eh_E+h_Ed_E$. Thus a homotopy inverse for $I(f)$ induces homotopy inverses on $C,E,B$ and the shifted cone, and inclusion $c\mapsto(0,c)$ commutes with these maps. Both sides and their comparison therefore invert quasi-isomorphisms of $K$ and descend through localization. Combining this quasi-isomorphism with step 4 gives the asserted natural isomorphism in $D(A)$.
